label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate with Moderate Screen Use
summary: This profile represents a group of 125 respondents characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score averages 0.79 (well below typical thresholds), PHQ-9 depression averages 0.28, and GAD-7 anxiety averages near zero at 0.04. These individuals appear to be psychologically well-adjusted with minimal mental health burden, suggesting strong social connectedness and emotional stability.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with daily screen/internet usage of 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness levels suggesting robust social connections and support networks
Near-floor depressive symptom scores indicating positive mood and functional well-being
Essentially negligible anxiety symptoms pointing to effective stress management
Moderate and controlled screen use (1–3 hours daily) rather than excessive digital engagement
Higher educational attainment potentially associated with greater coping resources and health literacy

label: Digitally Over-Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on digital devices and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (mean ≈ 1.66), PHQ-9 depression score (mean ≈ 1.65), and GAD-7 anxiety score (mean ≈ 2.10) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. With 198 respondents in this cluster, the profile represents a sizable subgroup where prolonged screen time coincides with compounded emotional difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily screen use (more than 5 hours)
Elevated loneliness scores indicating perceived social isolation despite digital connectivity
Moderate-to-high depressive symptom endorsement on PHQ-9 items
Notably high anxiety symptom levels (highest among the three distress indicators)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting a compounded distress pattern
tone: Concerned and empathetic, highlighting the convergence of multiple psychological stressors in a high-screen-time, highly educated female population

label: Well-Adjusted Female Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.21, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.79, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating generally positive mental well-being.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Demonstrates low anxiety levels well below clinical concern
Maintains moderate and controlled screen or internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
Likely benefits from strong social connectedness and educational resources associated with advanced education
